nfr_posture.requirement: F1's initial migration is reversible (PI5); later additive migrations preserve stock_records rows. The immutable timestamp+actor audit governs inventory ADJUSTMENTS, which F1 does not introduce (F2-F5) – N/A for F1 beyond reversibility.
A filed quantity is never negative: rejected at the boundary (422 naming quantity) and by CHECK quantity >= 0. Overcommit/pick is N/A in F1 (no pick operation until F3).
Each (sku, location) is uniquely addressable; a re-file is resolved at write time by an atomic upsert, never a duplicate or an error page. location is stored verbatim (canonical).
Acceptance/integration tests run against the paired Lakebase branch via DATABASE_URL; no mock, stub, sqlite or in-memory substitute.
The UI is the React SPA under client/; the boundary returns JSON only (renders_via react). Form submits are async with no full-page reload.
F1 has no barcode-scan interaction (N/A until scan-driven forms land); the write endpoint stays well inside the budget so later scan UX is not blocked.
Validation errors name the offending field and render inline next to it; never a generic 'bad request'. Status->text mapping goes through the client describeError() helper.
F1's migration is purely additive (a new table); no existing table is altered or dropped.
Omitted optional detail is stored as NULL (never '' or a placeholder) so S2/S3 can render 'not tracked' per field; the rendering half is owned by S2/S3's ACs.
N/A for F1 – search/filter is explicitly F9 (out of scope). F1 only ensures the stock_records (sku, location) columns exist for F9 to index; F9 will declare the access_pattern.

invariant_patterns.brief: A composite UNIQUE (sku, location) constraint rejects a second row for the same pair; the write path upserts against it (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) so re-filing updates in place.
sku and location are NOT NULL: an insert omitting either is rejected by the database.
CHECK (quantity >= 0): a direct insert/update with a negative quantity is rejected by the database.

The initial create_table migration is reversible: downgrade to its down_revision drops stock_records, and upgrade head recreates the table with its columns, UNIQUE (sku, location), NOT NULL and CHECK constraints present again (schema recreated; no data survival implied).
